title: Know what to do
subtitle: Read these guides before an earthquake. Practise the steps with your family. Pages you opened before work without internet.

drop.text: Go down on your hands and knees. Then the shaking cannot knock you down.

cover.text: Cover your head and neck. Go under a strong table if one is near.

hold.text: Hold on to the table. If the table moves, move with it.

dch.noTable: No table near you? Go down next to an inside wall. Cover your head and neck with your arms.
dch.stay: Stay in this position until the shaking stops.

kitChecklist.saved: Tick each item when it is in your kit. Your ticks stay on this device only.

before.title: Before an earthquake
before.description: Make your home safer and make a plan with your family.

secureHome.title: Make your home safer
points: Attach tall cabinets, shelves and heavy furniture to the wall.
Put latches on cabinet doors. Then the contents cannot fall out.
Put heavy items on low shelves.
Keep glass and other items that can break in closed cabinets.
Do not hang heavy frames or mirrors above beds or seats.

emergencyPlanning.title: Make a family plan
points: Choose a place where your family will meet after an earthquake.
Find a safe spot in each room, such as under a strong table.
Practise Drop, Cover, Hold on with your family.
Write down emergency numbers. Keep them near the phone and in your wallet.
Know the way to your barangay evacuation area. Walk it with your family.

importantDocuments.title: Keep your papers safe
points: Keep copies of important papers in a waterproof bag.
Include IDs, land titles, insurance papers and medical records.
Take photos of your home and your things.
Keep some cash. ATMs may not work after an earthquake.

during.title: During the shaking
during.description: Drop, Cover, Hold on. Do it at once when the ground shakes.

indoors.title: If you are inside
points: Stay inside. Do not run outside while the ground shakes.
Do not stand in a doorway. It is not safer than other places.
Stay away from windows, glass and tall furniture.
Do not use the elevator.
If you are in bed, stay there. Cover your head with a pillow.

outdoors.title: If you are outside
points: Move away from buildings, walls, trees and power lines.
Drop, Cover, Hold on in an open area.
If you drive, stop in a safe place. Stay in the vehicle.
Do not stop on or under bridges, overpasses or power lines.

nearCoast.title: If you are near the sea
points: If the shaking is strong or long, go to high ground at once.
Do not wait for an official warning.
If the sea goes back far from the shore, go to high ground.
Stay away from the shore until officials say it is safe.

after.title: After the shaking
after.description: Check for injuries and danger. Expect aftershocks.

immediate.title: First steps
points: Check yourself and others for injuries. Give first aid if you know how.
Look for danger: gas leaks, broken wires and damage to the building.
If you smell gas, close the LPG tank valve. Open the windows and go outside.
Use a flashlight. Do not use candles or matches.
Expect aftershocks. Drop, Cover, Hold on again when they come.

communication.title: Get information
points: Listen to the radio for official news and instructions.
Send text messages. Make calls only for emergencies.
Check on your neighbours. Help older people and people with disabilities first.
Stay off the roads. Leave them for emergency vehicles.
Do not go into damaged buildings.

ongoingSafety.title: In the days after
points: Check your home for damage before you go back inside.
Take photos of the damage for insurance or aid claims.
Emergency services can be very busy. Be patient.
Save phone battery and water.
Help others if you can do it safely.

kit.title: Emergency go bag
kit.description: Pack supplies for at least 3 days. Keep the bag near the door.

items.water: About 4 litres of water for each person for each day
items.food: Food that does not spoil, such as canned goods and biscuits
items.babyFood: Milk and food for babies, if you need them

items.powerBank: A charged power bank and a phone cable
items.whistle: A whistle to call for help

items.hygiene: Soap, toothbrush, sanitary pads and tissue
items.dustMask: Face masks to keep out dust

items.documents: Copies of IDs and important papers in a waterproof bag
items.cash: Cash in small bills and coins
items.clothes: A change of clothes and a blanket

building.title: A safer building
building.description: A strong building protects the people inside it.

foundation.title: Structure
points: Ask a licensed civil engineer to check older buildings.
Build and repair to the National Structural Code of the Philippines.
Hollow block walls must have steel bars inside.
Look for cracks in walls, posts and beams. Get them repaired.
Check the roof, posts and beams regularly.

interior.title: Inside the home
points: Close the LPG tank valve when you do not use the stove.
Use a good gas hose and check it for cracks.
Attach ceiling fans and lights tightly.
Put safety film on large windows.
Fix small items in place with putty or straps.

community.title: Your community
community.description: Neighbours help each other first after a disaster.

neighborhood.title: With your neighbours
points: Join the earthquake drills in your barangay, school or office.
Know which neighbours have medical or building skills.
Make a plan for older people and people with disabilities.
Agree how you will contact each other after an earthquake.

resources.title: Know your area
points: Know where your evacuation area, hospital and health centre are.
Ask your barangay hall about emergency supplies.
Learn the emergency plan of your barangay and city.
Take a first aid course, for example with the Philippine Red Cross.
Support safe building rules in your community.
